name: Lord Shiva
description: The Destroyer of evil and the Transformer within the Trimurti. He is the patron god of yoga, meditation, and arts.

stories.title: The Churning of the Ocean (Samudra Manthan)
stories.content: During the churning of the cosmic ocean, a deadly poison (Halahala) emerged that threatened to destroy all creation. To protect the universe, Lord Shiva swallowed the poison, holding it in his throat. This turned his neck blue, earning him the name Neelkanth.

symbolism.description: Represents wisdom and the destruction of ignorance.
Adorning his head, it signifies control over time and the cycles of nature.

name: Lord Ganesha
description: The Elephant-headed deity, known as the Remover of Obstacles, the patron of arts and sciences, and the Deva of intellect and wisdom.

stories.title: The Race Around the Universe
stories.content: Ganesha and his brother Kartikeya were challenged to race around the universe. While Kartikeya flew off on his peacock, Ganesha walked around his parents, Lord Shiva and Goddess Parvati, declaring that they represented the entire universe to him. Moved by his wisdom, they declared him the winner.

symbolism.description: Symbolizes immense wisdom, foresight, and listening ability.

name: Lord Hanuman
description: The loyal devotee of Lord Rama, representing strength, devotion, humility, and selflessness.

stories.title: Lifting the Dronagiri Mountain
stories.content: When Lord Rama's brother Lakshmana was mortally wounded during the battle in Lanka, Hanuman was sent to fetch the Sanjeevani herb from the Himalayas. Unable to identify the herb, Hanuman lifted the entire Dronagiri mountain and carried it back to the battlefield, saving Lakshmana's life.

symbolism.description: Reveals images of Rama and Sita, signifying absolute and unwavering devotion.

name: Goddess Durga
description: The protective mother goddess representing the divine feminine strength (Shakti), protector of the righteous and destroyer of demonic forces.
weapon: Trishula, Shankha, Chakra, Bow and Arrow

stories.title: Defeat of Mahishasura
stories.content: The buffalo demon Mahishasura unleashed terror on Earth and Heaven. Since a boon prevented his defeat by any man or god, the trinity combined their energies to manifest Goddess Durga. She fought him for nine days and nights, ultimately decapitating him with her trident.

symbolism.description: Represents protection from all ten directions of the universe.

name: Lord Krishna
description: The eighth avatar of Lord Vishnu, the god of love, compassion, tenderness, playfulness, and the speaker of the Bhagavad Gita.

stories.title: Lifting the Govardhan Hill
stories.content: To protect the villagers of Vrindavan from torrents of rain sent by the angry rain god Indra, Lord Krishna lifted the Govardhan Hill on his little finger, providing a giant umbrella for the people and animals for seven days.

symbolism.description: Symbolizes beauty, purity, and the vibrant colors of nature and cosmic creation.

name: Lord Rama
description: The seventh avatar of Lord Vishnu, the prince and king of Ayodhya, representing the ideal human and embodiment of righteousness (Dharma).

stories.title: Building the Ram Setu Bridge
stories.content: To cross the ocean to Lanka to rescue his wife Sita, Rama's vanara army built a floating stone bridge. Each stone inscribed with Rama's name miraculously floated on water due to their devotion and the divine name's power.

symbolism.description: Symbolizes preparedness, focus, and targets aimed towards upholding righteousness.

name: Goddess Lakshmi
description: The goddess of wealth, fortune, power, beauty, fertility, and prosperity. She is the consort of Lord Vishnu.

stories.title: Emergence from the Milky Ocean
stories.content: During Samudra Manthan (churning of the ocean), Goddess Lakshmi emerged standing on a fully bloomed lotus. She chose Lord Vishnu as her eternal consort among all assembled gods due to his righteousness.

symbolism.description: Represents prosperity, both material and spiritual, flowing to devotees.

name: Goddess Saraswati
description: The goddess of knowledge, music, art, speech, wisdom, and learning. She is part of the Tridevi.

stories.title: Flowing as the River Saraswati
stories.content: Goddess Saraswati descended to Earth as a holy river of pure knowledge to cleanse the worlds, fertilize the plains, and inspire sages to compile the sacred scriptures.

symbolism.description: Represents the harmony of all creative arts, intellect, and speech.

name: Lord Vishnu
description: The Preserver and Protector of the universe, responsible for maintaining balance and upholding Dharma.

stories.title: The Ten Avatars (Dashavatara)
stories.content: Whenever Dharma is threatened by evil, Lord Vishnu descends to Earth in various forms (avatars) to restore order. His most famous avatars include Rama and Krishna.

symbolism.description: Represents the infinite and all-pervading nature, like the sky or the ocean.

name: Lord Brahma
description: The Creator of the universe in the Hindu trinity (Trimurti). He created all living beings and the universe itself.

stories.title: Creation from the Lotus
stories.content: According to Puranic legends, Brahma was born from a lotus that emerged from the navel of Lord Vishnu.

symbolism.description: Represent the four Vedas, the four yugas (epochs), and the four directions.

name: Lord Surya
description: The Sun God, the supreme light and life-giver, revered for his energy and illumination.

stories.title: The Chariot
stories.content: Lord Surya rides a magnificent chariot driven by Aruna, pulled by seven horses representing the colors of the rainbow or the seven days of the week.

symbolism.description: Represent the seven chakras or the days of the week.
